name: Othniel and Achsah
charge: Taking Kirjath-sepher at Caleb’s word; and asking for the springs as well as the land
summary: Caleb, given Hebron for wholly following the Lord, drove out the three sons of Anak and offered his daughter to whoever smote Kirjath-sepher. Othniel the son of Kenaz, his younger brother, took it and was given Achsah. She moved him to ask her father for a field, and asked well: he had given her a south land, so she asked also for springs of water, and Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs. When Israel served Chushan-rishathaim eight years, the Spirit of the Lord came on Othniel, and he judged Israel and went out to war, for the Lord is a man of war.
offenseFull: Caleb the son of Jephunneh was given a part among the children of Judah according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua, the city of Arba the father of Anak, which is Hebron, and Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai (Joshua 15:13-14). He had been promised that mountain and he went and claimed it. He went up from there against the inhabitants of Debir, whose name before was Kirjath-sepher, and promised his daughter Achsah as wife to the man who smote it and took it; Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s brother, took it, and Caleb gave him Achsah (Joshua 15:15-17). He took a fortified city on the strength of a word.

Achsah’s obedience is one of speech. When she came to him she moved him to ask her father for a field, then got down off her ass, and when Caleb asked what she wanted she asked for a blessing, because he had given her a south land, and asked also for springs of water (Joshua 15:18-19). Given a lawful portion in the dry south, she did not resent it; she asked the right person, at the right moment, framing it as a blessing rather than a complaint, and asked for the one thing the land needed. The record carries the whole account twice, at the opening of Judges as at the end of Joshua, because the history is worth reviewing (Judges 1:12-15).
judgmentFull: Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs (Joshua 15:19): more than she had asked for. Then the Lord left nations in the land to prove Israel, nations that had not known the wars of Canaan, so that the generations of the children of Israel might know war and be taught it, and so that it would be seen whether they would hearken to His commandments (Judges 3:1-4). They did not. The children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, the very people they had been told to destroy, took their daughters to wife and gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods; so the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel and He sold them into the hand of Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia, whom they served eight years (Judges 3:5-8).

When the children of Israel cried to the Lord, He raised up a deliverer, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother; the Spirit of the Lord came on him, and he judged Israel and went out to war, and the Lord delivered Chushan-rishathaim into his hand, and his hand prevailed (Judges 3:9-10). He judged Israel, and today our people say that no one can judge them. And he went out to war, because the Lord is a man of war, and that is His name (Exodus 15:3); that also answers the question asked of the men out on the street about where their women are. The war now is spiritual: though we walk in the flesh we do not war after the flesh, and the weapons of our warfare are not carnal but mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds, casting down imaginations and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God (2 Corinthians 10:3-5). The weapon is this Bible. The land had rest forty years, until Othniel the son of Kenaz died (Judges 3:11). The first deliverer in the book of Judges came out of the household of the man who wholly followed the Lord, where a daughter asked well and a father gave more than was requested.

text.text: And unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a part among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua, even the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron.
And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.
And he went up thence to the inhabitants of Debir: and the name of Debir before was Kirjath–sepher.
And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.
And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.
And it came to pass, as she came unto him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she lighted off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wouldest thou?
Who answered, Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs.
And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.
And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.
And it came to pass, when she came to him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she lighted from off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wilt thou?
And she said unto him, Give me a blessing: for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.
Who answered, Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs.
Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan;
Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof;
Namely, five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites that dwelt in mount Lebanon, from mount Baal–hermon unto the entering in of Hamath.
And they were to prove Israel by them, to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
And the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Hivites, and Jebusites:
And they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgat the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves.
Therefore the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushan–rishathaim king of Mesopotamia: and the children of Israel served Chushan–rishathaim eight years.
And when the children of Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord raised up a deliverer to the children of Israel, who delivered them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.

And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war: and the Lord delivered Chushan–rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand; and his hand prevailed against Chushan–rishathaim.
The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.
For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh:
(For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)
Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ;
And the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
